title: 'Yellowstone' star is living in a camper on her Arkansas ranch
text:

 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage 'Yellowstone' star is living in a camper on her Arkansas ranch
 Sameen Chaudhry, USA TODAY Updated Wed, 11 November 2026 at 3:14 pm UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Dawn Olivieri is willing to sell eggs at a roadside stand if it means keeping her freedom.
 The "Yellowstone" actress says she wound up booking more acting jobs after moving to an Arkansas ranch than she had in Los Angeles. 
 Olivieri, 45, said a stretch between jobs left her tired of waiting for someone else to decide when she could work , she told Fox News Digital in a Nov. 10 interview ⁠.
 "I realized it wasn't giving me what my dream of what it was supposed to give me," Olivieri said. "I didn't have offers, just like falling out of my phone. I went through a dry spell, and I was like, 'Wow, so this is an illusion.' I kind of saw through the veil and once I saw through veil – I realized in that moment, I have to make some decisions about my life that makes me happy – [it] isn't always waiting by the phone, losing my power, waiting for someone to hire me."
 Dawn Olivieri attends the "Homestead" premiere on Dec. 10, 2024, in Los Angeles. Kevin Costner's dark 'Yellowstone' fate turns Beth Dutton into 'a hurricane' 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As taped auditions became routine during the pandemic, Olivieri got a nudge from her mother. "You don't have to live in L.A. to be an actress," Olivieri recalled her saying in a 2023 interview with The Hollywood Reporter ⁠. 
 She asked herself what she would do with the money if the offers started coming in. 
 "Well, I would move to the country and have horses," she said. "And so I did that with nothing. Which wasn't the dream part, but in actuality, it was what was always meant to happen because I moved toward my own authenticity."
 In 2022, she bought 160-acre property near Mena, Arkansas, and said goodbye to her life in Los Angeles, according to Fox News . 
 Gene Hackman retired from acting in 2004, announcing his decision to step away in an interview with Larry King. He became a novelist and a painter after leaving Hollywood behind. 
 (HECTOR MATA, AFP/Getty Images) Gene Hackman is best known for roles in "Bonnie and Clyde," "The French Connection" and "Hoosiers" (pictured here). (MARY ANN CARTER, MGM) Jack Gleeson is best known for his role as King Joffrey in "Game of Thrones." But he's sick of acting.  (Macall B. Polay, HBO) Bynes' last movie role was "Easy A" in 2010. She's also well-known for starring in "She's the Man," "What a Girl Wants" and "The Amanda Show."  (Rob McEwan, DreamWorks Pictures) Redford told Entertainment Weekly in 2018 that he was fairly certain he was done acting: "Never say never, but I pretty well concluded that this would be it for me in terms of acting ... I've been doing it since I was 21." He died in 2025 at age 89.
 (KENA BETANCUR, AFP/Getty Images) Daniel Day-Lewis' won Oscars for his roles in "Lincoln," "There Will Be Blood" and "My Left Foot." His nominations include "Phantom Thread" (pictured here). 
 (Laurie Sparham, Focus Features) After completing "Phantom Thread" in 2017, Day-Lewis announced he would retire from acting: "All my life, I've mouthed off about how I should stop acting," he told W Magazine. "I don't know why it was different this time, but the impulse to quit took root in me and that became a compulsion. It was something I had to do." In 2025, he returned to star in son Ronan Day-Lewis' movie "Anemone."
 (Lars Niki, Getty Images for the Academy) Connery retired following his role in 2003's "The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen." He died 17 years later, in 2020, at age 90.
 (Clive Brunskill, Getty Images) Cameron Diaz was a big-screen staple in the late 1990s and the first decade of 2000 with movies like "There's Something About Mary," "Shrek" and "Charlie's Angels."   (DARREN MICHAELS, SONY) She came out of retirement to star with Jamie Foxx in 2025's "Back in Action," her first film role since 2014.
 (John Wilson/Netflix) Aussie Portia de Rossi broke through in America with the late-'90s legal TV dramedy "Ally McBeal." Later, she became a part of the Bluth clan on the cult comedy "Arrested Development."  But it sounds like she might be done. (DAN MACMEDAN, USA TODAY) Stars who quit Hollywood: Daniel Day-Lewis, Cameron Diaz and more

 (HECTOR MATA, AFP/Getty Images) Kevin Costner explains leaving 'Yellowstone': A return was 'not in the cards' 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Olivieri played Claire Dutton in Taylor Sheridan's "1883" before joining "Yellowstone" as Sarah Atwood⁠, the lawyer who gets involved with Wes Bentley's Jamie Dutton. She now plays Jenna Ross on "Homestead: The Series," which returned for its second season in November. 
 Inside Dawn Olivieri's Arkansas horse rescue
 In August 2023, Olivieri and her social media followers raised money to rescue mares and foals that were being held for slaughter. Within a month, they were caring for 50 horses, according to Moon Mountain Sanctuary and Rescue ⁠, the nonprofit she founded at her ranch. 
 Dawn Olivieri attends Paramount Network's "Yellowstone" SAG event at SAG-AFTRA on Jan. 6, 2023, in Los Angeles. On the Aug. 12 episode of the "Let's Talk Local" podcast,⁠ Olivieri told host Sarah Zubiate Bennett she was living in a camper on the ranch.
 Olivieri told Fox she'd come to think of Arkansas as "a land of no mirrors." On the ranch, she said, she spent less time worrying about how she looked and more time getting to know herself. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I became a better actress for sure," she said.
